title: WALL Pattern: Workflow At-a-glance, Live & Legible — a process wall format and renderer
description: Most dashboards answer how a process is doing; people who run a process ask where work is stuck and what changed. WALL Pattern is an open pattern, format and renderer for that second question, in the spirit of an andon board: grey is normal, and colour appears only where a step needs attention. A wall is two JSON files. wall.config.json declares the structure (steps, hero indicators and thresholds, connectors, return loops, exceptions, display) and changes rarely; wall.feed.json reports only what is true now (values, flows, oldest-item ages, open exceptions). The feed carries no deltas: the renderer, a single self-contained HTML file with no build step, keeps the previous snapshot and the baseline for the current shift, day or week and computes what changed. Both files are specified as JSON Schema 2020-12. Version 0.2 adds a delta window (shift, day or week) that resets the baseline when a new period starts, quieter connector labels, stall labels on their own line, a fuller exceptions panel, and drops a redundant ring line in the orbit layout. It is a working renderer (row and orbit layouts, deltas coloured by meaning, stall rules, exceptions, change log, kiosk mode, URL parameters, drop-in and watched feed files) and a schema-validated contract, with fictional examples and one real wall run on a case-review cycle. Known gaps are listed in the README. No research claim is made.
